correctness.rationale: Terminal maximality gives only sizes three and four by an elementary classification of pairwise intersecting edges of K5. The memoryless exponential-race recursion is exact. A complete 52-state rational-function computation separately evaluates adjacent and nonadjacent cases and checks exact symbolic cancellation; an independent 8! times 90 marked-position enumeration per case validates the probability law at six positive rational pairs. The proof concerns exactly one finite 10-vertex graph, so there is no unproved infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: On the evidence inspected, general graph adsorption, large random graph greedy limits and finite dimer deposition do not imply the displayed two-rate Petersen vertex-monomer law or its adjacent/nonadjacent sign reversal. An older broad regular-graph paper was abstract-only, and historical novelty is provisional. The accessible related all-N two-subset Kneser adsorption theorem with one fully star-biased rate does supply the maximal-family classification and homogeneous Petersen baseline, which are credited as prior facts; its four simultaneously marked sites at N=5 do not imply the two independently tunable marked-site response.

value.rationale: Two-site rate perturbation is the first nontrivial response of a vertex-transitive greedy hard-core deposition system, since changing a single priority distribution cannot affect an invariant terminal statistic. The result gives the entire terminal-size distribution for arbitrary positive site rates on the canonical cubic girth-five cage and establishes opposite strict effects for its two pair orbits and a universal -2 ratio. This precisely measures geometry-controlled nonadditive kinetic interference, beyond simply recomputing the unbiased finite count.
